picks.title: How to Put Your Design System to Work With the Figma Agent
picks.excerpt: Your design system can help the Figma agent understand the principles and guidelines that define your product. Here’s to make that context useful to the agent.
picks.rationale: An official Figma guide to feeding design-system context to the Figma agent. Teams can apply it tomorrow. It is a different post from the 10-07 '3 ways' use-case piece and the 10-07 dev.to Claude Code test.

picks.title: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
picks.excerpt: Anthropic unveiled Claude Duet, a new AI agent positioned against Meta's Muse; a waitlist is open now. You can get on the waitlist now for Duet.
picks.rationale: A new agent product launch from a major lab, with the waitlist open now. The history covers Muse Charm (09-27) and the Instinct/Muse/Dots hands-on (10-10), but Duet itself is a new release.

picks.title: New PTC Jetstream brings collaboration layer to Windchill
picks.excerpt: PTC Jetstream is a cloud collaboration layer connecting product development teams, review meetings and context in an AI-native layer
picks.rationale: A new product launch from a major PLM vendor: an AI-native collaboration layer on top of Windchill. It was chosen over the Siemens EDA and CloudNC quoting items because it is closer to how product designers work.

picks.title: Can you take AI at its word?
picks.excerpt: Dora Czerna on the psychology of trusting AI output, and what UX designers should do about confident-sounding AI answers.
picks.rationale: Practical UX guidance on designing around AI answers that sound confident: how to signal uncertainty and calibrate user trust. It is a fresh angle next to the 10-08 bounded-delegation and 10-11 'show me what it can change' pieces, and it replaces the Etsy pick, which marketing owns today.

picks.title: Buy vs. build is now also a UX decision, especially in enterprise
picks.excerpt: AI made building cheap and buying easy; Patrick Neeman argues the trade-off now turns on who owns upkeep, the seams between tools, chat surfaces and data, making it a UX call.
picks.rationale: Reframes the AI-era buy-vs-build choice as a design decision (upkeep ownership, seams between tools, chat surfaces), which helps designers argue for their seat in tooling decisions. It replaces the vendor-written Tripo/80 Level piece. It is the second workflow pick, so it takes palette accent #3b6bff.

dedup.note: Re-curation after the cross-section check. Two picks were replaced. (1) The Etsy AI-slop listings piece (The Verge) was removed because the same Etsy AI-policy story is published in marketing today. (2) The 80 Level 'Tripo P2.0 & Astra in Blender and Unity' piece was removed because the Tripo team wrote it (vendor advertorial), and the games curator rejected it for the same reason. The replacements are two UX Collective essays: 'Can you take AI at its word?' and 'Buy vs. build is now also a UX decision'. Neither appears in the 30-day history_digest, and neither has a history_match. The Canva first-image-model story is not in today's pool, and it was already published in design on 10-23 (theverge.com/.../canva-craft-in-house-ai-model), so it would be a repeat anyway. Other candidates stay excluded. Wildwood/LAIKA belongs to movies. The Builder.io AI Agent Actions essay is a follow-up to the 10-15 Agent-Native launch with no new release. The Figma YouTube AI-credits video is the same source and core topic as the Figma Blog agent pick (content hub). NVIDIA Spark Europe, Cosmos and Isaac, plus the ASUS ProArt P16 review, are compute or hardware noise and related to the 10-14 and 10-22 NVIDIA posts. The Fast Company Unitree H2-X critique is robotics hardware with a weak design-workflow angle, and it is a possible gadgets clash. The rest were skipped on score: Matt Wolfe's roundup, Vercel Agent production access, the Siemens 3D IC EDA workflow, CloudNC Quote Agent, the UX Collective founder essay and Creative Bloq's Draco Malfoy piece. Final 5: four outlets (Figma Blog, The Verge, DEVELOP3D, UX Collective x2, within the 2-per-outlet cap) and four categories (figma, workflow x2, cad, tokens). No URL repeats. The Duet pick is still reserved for design; music skips it.
